result.final_text:
## What this letter says
This letter gives your test results. You had a camera test of the stomach (gastroscopy). Small samples were taken (biopsies) on 8 September 2026.

- The samples show no cancer (no evidence of malignancy).
- There is no sign of a stomach germ (Helicobacter pylori infection).
- The samples show a change in the lining of your stomach (intestinal metaplasia). This is not cancer.
- In a few people, this change can grow over many years. So the doctors keep an eye on it.

## What you need to do
1. Continue to take omeprazole.
2. Stop taking ibuprofen and other anti-inflammatory painkillers. They can irritate the stomach.
3. You can use paracetamol instead.
4. You do not need to do anything now about the next gastroscopy. The hospital will send you an appointment.

## Dates and medicines
- 8 September 2026: gastroscopy and biopsies.
- September 2029: repeat gastroscopy planned (in 3 years).
- Omeprazole: 20 milligrams, once daily. Continue.
- Ibuprofen and similar painkillers: stop.
- Paracetamol: you can use it instead. No dose is given.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- How will you watch the change in my stomach lining?
- Which painkillers must I stop?
- How much paracetamol can I use?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
